_readme: The two calibration sets of COLLECTION.md §4, pre-registered before the base build and cleared before the grind writes any verdict. Keys are external documents where one exists; a row that could not be anchored at reasonable cost is NOT in the key -- it is listed under `unresolved` and goes to the grind as a row needing its own citation, which is the honest treatment and keeps the key from being padded with model opinion.

stage_golden_set._purpose:
Measure the two INDEPENDENT first-party entry-round layers this firm publishes, blind, before either may label a row (decisions.md R1). Layer A = the live Sanity CMS `stage` enum, on all 277 live rows. Layer B = the

round ladder on the 2011-2019 archived listings, on 151 rows; its first element is the entry.
stage_golden_set._taxonomy_note: Answers are the PUBLISHED taxonomy (Pre-Seed | Seed | Series A | Growth), not the round word. Growth absorbs Series B and everything later, so a B-vs-C disagreement between the layers is not a taxonomy miss and is not scored as one. On the 56 rows both layers cover, they agree on 53 after that mapping.
stage_golden_set._size_note: 18 rows, below the playbook's 30-40 target, and the reason is a property of this investor rather than of the effort spent: Felicis publishes no first-party announcement archive (its blog is a curated feed of third-party press clippings -- 246 posts, only 19 naming a round), and only 17 company records carry prose stating the entry round. Rows were added only where a document answers; four more were attempted and left unresolved. The gate compensates by requiring layer AGREEMENT rather than promoting a single layer on a thin key -- see `scoring_rule`.
stage_golden_set._scoring_rule: Score each layer separately against the key. A layer may be promoted to class 1 only where it clears the key AND the other layer agrees on the row; rows where the two layers disagree are class 3 at best and go to the judge with a citation attempt regardless of either layer's score.

unresolved.why: Press places Felicis in the Oct-2015 $80M Series C; one vendor profile claims a July-2014 seed entry. Contemporaneous press does not settle it and the two first-party layers disagree, so the row is excluded from the key and goes to the grind for its own citation.

TechCrunch's Nov-2009 report names Felicis in the $2.5M Series A led by QED; a vendor profile claims a first investment at the Apr-2013 Series B; the circles ladder is [Seed, Series A, Series B], implying an entry before the A. Three sources, three answers -- judged on its own evidence.
